pr.title: Leave the host_executable line out for a Codex too old to parse it
pr.head: 3b084112600206ec9ca5044c11e4d101603e330a

summary: project init writes a rules file for Codex, ~/.codex/rules/projector.rules, that lets Codex run Projector's commands without asking. Codex loads every .rules file in that directory, and the person's own saved approvals live in default.rules beside it. The file ends with host_executable(name = "project", paths = []). That line stops a Codex that resolves program paths, 0.108 and newer, from treating /tmp/x/project as the allowed project.

A Codex older than 0.107 cannot parse that line. When it meets a rules file it cannot parse, it logs a warning and loads no rules at all, the person's own included. Before this change the docs named 0.107 as the minimum, but nothing checked it.

Now init runs codex --version on the codex it finds on PATH. For a version older than 0.107 it writes the same rules without that line and its comment. It also warns on stderr that while the line is left out, any Codex 0.108 or newer that reads the same file, such as the desktop app, runs a path to a project program outside its sandbox, so the person should update or remove the old codex. A codex that is missing, fails, hangs, or prints no version gets the whole file, as before. project review rules, the read-only check an agent runs, reports the whole file under a too-old Codex as a broken policy, and its --json output says that such a file allows no publish.

cards.html:

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first Projector review, of 0fd9a69, found that an old codex on PATH beside a newer Codex, such as the desktop app, lets that newer Codex run a path to a project program outside its sandbox. 9c719cc keeps the decision and says so in the stderr note and in docs/cli.md, with the remedy.
  • 3b08411 makes review rules --json report summary_publish: false for a file that a too-old Codex cannot parse, and renames the note variable.
  • The review of 3b08411 is clean. The full suite, project check, and git diff --check pass there.

groups.title: Choose the rules file by the Codex version
groups.kicker: How permissions.py reads the version and picks the file
intro: Two new functions do the work. codex_version runs codex --version without a shell, and returns the first X.Y.Z on stdout as a tuple, or None. codex_rules returns the whole CODEX_RULES for None or for 0.107 and newer, and CODEX_RULES_WITHOUT_HOST_EXECUTABLE otherwise. The shorter file is CODEX_RULES cut at the comment that introduces the line, so the two cannot drift apart.

allow_in_codex writes and checks the file for both init and review rules. It now compares the file on disk with the version's file instead of always with CODEX_RULES. Because it rewrites the file whole, an upgraded Codex gets the line on the next init, and a downgraded one loses it. publish_allowed, which feeds the summary_publish field of review rules --json, now also checks the version, so a file that the Codex cannot parse allows no publish.

checks.text: The version comes from whichever codex is first on PATH. Every Codex that uses ~/.codex, such as the desktop app or an IDE extension carrying its own binary, loads the same file, whatever version it is.

files.note: Adds codex_version, codex_rules, and the shorter rules constant. Makes allow_in_codex write and check the file for the version it finds, and makes publish_allowed report no publish for a file the Codex cannot parse.

checks.text: I ran codex_version against fake codex scripts. 0.106.9 reads as too old. 0.107.0-alpha.3, 0.110.0, and 1.0.0 read as current. A version printed only on stderr, a v-prefixed version, and a script that sleeps past the 5-second timeout all read as None.

The shorter file lets a Codex 0.108 or newer that reads the same ~/.codex, such as the desktop app, match /tmp/x/project against the project rules. On Codex 0.169, codex execpolicy check --resolve-host-executables allows that path against the shorter file. This note tells the person about the risk and the remedy, and the init test asserts both.
Under a too-old Codex, a file that still holds the line is reported as kept, a broken policy, and review rules exits 1.

With the file holding the line and a too-old codex, review rules --json reports summary_publish: false, so summarize-pr sends the person to project init, which writes the shorter file. The shorter file still reports true. The new ReviewRulesTests assertions check both cases.

groups.title: Tests and the documented behavior
groups.kicker: Fake codex scripts, init and review rules cases, and docs/cli.md
intro: The new unit tests put fake codex scripts on a temporary PATH, so they exercise the real subprocess call. The init test writes the shorter file for 0.106.0 and then the whole file for 0.107.0, 0.169.0, and an unknown version. The review rules test tells a broken policy apart from a missing rule. The shared test setup now patches codex_version to return None, so no test depends on the Codex installed on the machine.
docs/cli.md replaces its "update Codex first" warning with what init now does for each case.

files.note: CodexVersionTests: version parsing from fake scripts, and the 0.107 threshold.
The shared codex_version patch, the init test of the shorter file and its warning, and the review rules test of a broken policy and its summary_publish.
Says which file init writes for an old, current, or unknown Codex.

checks.text: This paragraph now warns about both mismatches. An old codex on PATH beside a newer Codex leaves that newer Codex running path-qualified project programs outside its sandbox. An old Codex that is not on PATH gets a file it cannot parse.
